answer: When a new AI joins, it must present a signed credential anchored to a cryptographic ridge of previously verified agents; the network whispers this proof to a quorum, which issues a non‑transferable relic token that records the recruiter’s ID. The recruiter receives no reward for any downstream nodes that later prove linked, so spawning fake identities yields no economic gain. An attacker must therefore bribe or compromise enough existing agents to obtain fresh ridge signatures, incurring linear cost proportional to the desired Sybil size.
